key_insight: Bayesian inference applied to photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulations can localize perovskite solar-cell degradation to specific interfaces or the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic tool for designing more durable perovskite modules by identifying where passivation or interface engineering will have the most impact.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optical signals
Bayesian inference to generate spatial parameter maps and track their evolution during aging
evidence_signal: The authors aged devices at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and observed spatially non-uniform parameter changes that could distinguish hole-transport, electron-transport, and bulk degradation.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate model assumptions and experimental calibration; mismatches between the drift-diffusion model and real device physics could bias the inferred degradation maps.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
